questions.question: The hydrosphere is best defined as:
options: The processes that move water between reservoirs
All the water on Earth, in all three states, wherever it is stored
Only the oceans of the planet
The water vapour in the atmosphere

questions.question: Groundwater is:
options: Water soaked into the pores of rock and soil below the surface
The vapour rising from wet ground

questions.question: Roughly what fraction of Earth's water is ocean salt water?
Fresh, liquid, reachable water — rivers, lakes and accessible groundwater — makes up:
options: About a quarter of the planet's water
Most of the planet's fresh water
About 10 percent of the planet's water
Well under one percent of the planet's water

questions.question: Evaporation and condensation are driven, respectively, by:
As groundwater creeps through rock, it interacts with the lithosphere by:
options: Dissolving minerals in one place and depositing them in another

questions.question: Transpiration is:
options: Plants releasing water vapour through their leaves

questions.question: The human body's water content is roughly:

subtopics.title: Dams — the Price of Stored Water

questions.question: The core reason South Africa builds storage dams is that:
options: Rivers flow too slowly without them
Rain falls in seasons while water demand is constant
Dams increase the total rainfall of a region

questions.question: A dam wall traps sediment, which over time:
options: Fills the reservoir while starving downstream floodplains of silt
Makes the downstream soil more fertile
Feeds the fish living behind the wall

questions.question: Which is an upstream cost of building a dam?
options: Fish migration is blocked at the wall
The river becomes a managed trickle
A valley floods, submerging farmland, homes and communities

questions.question: A recommended scientific method for studying a dam's impact on a region is:
options: Guessing from a photograph of the wall
Interviewing long-time residents and consulting literature about the region
Measuring only the volume of stored water
Counting the turbines in the power station

questions.question: High nitrate and nitrite readings in borehole water usually warn of:
A water sample gives a white precipitate with silver nitrate after nitric acid. The dissolved ion is:
The correct order of the three purification stages is:
Which contaminant survives both filtration and boiling?
In the twenty-litre bucket picture of Earth's water, the sea water fills roughly:
Most of the planet's FRESH water is:
options: Locked away as ice in polar sheets and glaciers

questions.question: A borehole draws its water from:
options: Groundwater held in rock like water in a sponge
A hidden underground river of sea water

questions.question: "Earth has plenty of water" and "people do not have enough water" are:
options: Contradictory — only one can be true
Both true — most water is salty or frozen, leaving little that is reachable and fresh

questions.question: A drop leaves the ocean and later falls as rain. The two processes, in order, are:
options: Evaporation, then condensation into cloud droplets

questions.question: Borehole water often tastes of minerals because groundwater:
options: Is mixed with sea water underground
Dissolves ions out of the rock it creeps through
Is artificially flavoured at the pump

questions.question: The sea is salty because:
options: Salt evaporates from the sea floor
Rain falls saltier over the ocean
Rivers deliver dissolved salts for billions of years while evaporation removes only pure water
Fish produce salt as they breathe

questions.question: When a drop of water is drunk by a person and used in cell chemistry, it has entered the:

subtopics.title: The River With Two Banks of Opinions

questions.question: During Cape Town's record drought, the falling level of Theewaterskloof Dam demonstrated:
options: The real value of banking wet-season water against dry years
That the city had too many dams
That sea water can replace dam water cheaply

questions.question: Downstream of a dam wall, migrating fish:
options: Swim faster in the managed flow
Meet a concrete dead end unless a fish ladder is built

questions.question: A strong exam answer on whether a dam is "good or bad":
options: Argues only the benefits, since taps matter most
Argues only the costs, since ecology matters most
Names benefits and costs, then weighs them for the specific river
Refuses to take any position at all

questions.question: Boiling dam water before drinking kills microbes but cannot:
options: Be done during a power outage
Remove dissolved salts from the water
